title: Cyclone & Severe Storm Safety Guide
summary: Cyclones bring destructive winds and storm surges. Secure your home, stay indoors in the strongest room, and avoid coastal regions.
precautions: Board up or tape windows and secure loose outdoor objects (furniture, roof sheets, signboards).
Disconnect electrical appliances and turn off gas cylinders.
Stock up on non-perishable food, fresh drinking water, and essential medicines for 3-5 days.
Stay indoors away from windows in an interior windowless room or bathroom.
Beware of the 'Eye of the Cyclone' — a temporary calm period followed by fierce winds from the opposite direction.
evacuation: If living in coastal low-lying areas or weak structures, evacuate early to official cyclone shelters.
Carry your emergency Go-Bag, warm clothes, and important documents.
Follow police and disaster management instruction routes strictly.
firstAid: Clean windblown debris cuts with clean water and antiseptic.
Treat head injuries from flying debris carefully; keep victim still and support the head.
Keep hypothermia victims warm using dry blankets.
emergencyChecklist: 3-day supply of drinking water and canned food
First aid kit and prescription medications
dos: DO remain indoors until official 'All Clear' is announced.
DO stay away from coastal waters and storm surge zones.
donts: DON'T go outside during the calm 'Eye of the Storm'.
DON'T touch fallen trees or downed electric wires.
DON'T venture into sea for fishing or sightseeing.
